instruction: Make Firefox your system's default browser on Ubuntu.

metadata.explanation: Task requires setting Firefox as the default web browser on Ubuntu. The evaluator uses a custom getter that queries xdg-mime for common web-related MIME types (text/html, application/xhtml+xml) and URL schemes (x-scheme-handler/http, x-scheme-handler/https) and returns the most common default application. The metric checks if the result includes 'firefox.desktop'. This task is similar in difficulty and complexity to the original VLC task, requiring the same type of system configuration change.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic correctly uses standard Linux xdg-mime tool to query default web browser settings
Comprehensive coverage: queries all major web-related MIME types (text/html, text/xml, application/xhtml+xml) and URL schemes (x-scheme-handler/http, x-scheme-handler/https)
Metric correctly handles expected.type='rule' parameter passing - directly accesses rules.get('include') as documented in guidance
Complete instruction coverage: evaluator verifies Firefox is set as default browser, which is exactly what the instruction requires
Correct expected value: 'firefox.desktop' is the standard Ubuntu desktop file identifier for Firefox
No UI dependency: verification queries persistent system settings directly, no postconfig needed
Good edge case handling: returns 'unknown' if no apps found, only appends truthy values to apps list
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: Verify that get_vm_command_line strips trailing whitespace/newlines from xdg-mime output to ensure clean string matching
Minor: Consider adding explicit string stripping in getter (line 30) to handle potential whitespace in command output: 'apps.append(app.strip())'
